title: Fasting is a shield
cue: What a fasting person says when insulted
arabic: الصِّيَامُ جُنَّةٌ فَلَا يَرْفُثْ وَلَا يَجْهَلْ وَإِنِ امْرُؤٌ قَاتَلَهُ أَوْ شَاتَمَهُ فَلْيَقُلْ إِنِّي صَائِمٌ مَرَّتَيْنِ
translation: Fasting is a shield, so let him not speak indecently or act ignorantly. If a man fights him or insults him, let him say: “I am fasting,” twice.

witnesses.name: dorar
witnesses.ref: dorar.net hadith encyclopedia: Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 1894, narrator Abu Hurayrah

provenance.note: The Arabic stored is the first part of the hadith, up to “twice”. The hadith continues with the fasting person’s breath and reward; that part is not quoted here. The chain of narrators is left out.
